label: Early input steps 1-2 for certain tokens (q,s,1,i,x,a,n,l,0,p); plus copy steps 1-2 of L=3 sequences
explanation: Two parts. (1) Original-phase steps t=1 and t=2 (about 71% of mass; 85% of activations fall there). Within those steps, whether it fires depends strongly on the input token: q fires most often (rate 0.28 overall, 22% of mass), then s, 1, i, x, a, n, l, 0, p. Other tokens rarely fire. (2) Copy-phase steps recall_idx 1 and 2 of length-3 sequences (t=4,5). These fire about 97% of the time and hold about 25% of mass, and the top activations sit here (max close to 0.147, e.g. y p z <DEL> [y] [p]). It never fires at the delimiter step, at t>=6 of the original phase, or in copy steps of sequences with L>=4 (apart from a few at recall_idx 3). It is weak at t=0 and t=3. First occurrences of a token are favoured. Residual misses are low-magnitude firings on other tokens at t=1-3. The token dependence is graded, so a hard token list caps precision at about 0.7.
